papers.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
papers.desc: Long-horizon search agents must make multiple sequential actions (steps) to search, retrieve, verify, and integrate evidence to reach a final answer.

papers.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
papers.desc: Agent self-evolution updates an agent's persistent state from prior experience and reuses it to solve related tasks more effectively.

papers.title: Ego2Robot: Scalable Robot Data Synthesis from Egocentric Human Data
papers.desc: Learning generalizable robot manipulation policies requires large-scale and diverse demonstration data.

papers.title: AVE-Compass: Towards Holistic Evaluation for Audio-Video Editing Abilities
papers.desc: While instruction-based video editing has advanced rapidly, real-world videos contain tightly coupled audio and visual signals, and editing one modality often requires coordinated changes in the other.

papers.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance
papers.desc: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a standard paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs).

papers.title: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
papers.desc: GUI agents must remember both useful experience from earlier tasks and unfinished progress in the current interaction.

papers.title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report
papers.desc: This technical report presents K-EXAONE 2.0, an open-weight multilingual foundation model developed by LG AI Research as a step in our effort toward global frontier-scale foundation models.

papers.title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models
papers.desc: Interactive video world models are essential for long-horizon planning and exploration, yet they suffer from compounding errors.

papers.title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation
papers.desc: Leveraging pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) to construct vision-language-action (VLA) models has emerged as a promising paradigm for 3D robot manipulation.

papers.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
papers.desc: Prompt injection poses significant security risks to LLM agents.

papers.title: Consistency-Driven Co-Evolution for Self-Supervised Cross-Representation Learning
papers.desc: As chart images, tabular data, and visualization code play increasingly important roles across diverse domains, cross-representation understanding across these modalities poses fundamental challenges for AI systems: the relationships across representations are inherently one-to-many, supervision is ambiguous and costly, and model optimization lacks a principled signal that is both direction-adaptive and representation-generalizable beyond task-specific objectives.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents
papers.desc: Large language models are increasingly embedded in software engineering workflows as coding agents that can inspect repositories, invoke tools, execute tests, debug failures, and generate patches.

papers.title: Lossless Tensor Compression as Program Synthesis
papers.desc: Model checkpoints are growing in both number and size, which makes archival, transfer, and deployment increasingly costly.

papers.title: DRIFT: Derailing Denoising Trajectories of Flow-Matching VLAs with Adversarial Patch Attack
papers.desc: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models such as pi0 generate robot actions by integrating a learned denoising velocity field, and have been reported to resist adversarial perturbations that readily fool autoregressive VLAs.

papers.title: Resume Means Resume: A Machine-Checked Conformance Contract for Checkpoint, Interrupt, and Resume Semantics in Workflow Persistence Layers
papers.desc: A framework that persists execution state so a run can be interrupted, survive a crash, and continue must decide what a resume means for effects that already fired.
